raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

With `--tool-call-parser deepseekv3`, when one stream increment carries two complete tool calls (a coalesced backlog from `_coalesce_streaming_chunks`, or a large `--stream-interval`), `parse_streaming_increment` emits only the second call, at `tool_index` 0. The first call never reaches the client.

Fixes #43523.

## Root cause

The streaming pattern anchors with greedy `(.*)` groups, so on a buffer with two calls it matches from the *last* `<｜tool▁sep｜>`: name and arguments come from the second call while the first is silently dropped. And even with correct anchoring, the old control flow returned after the first completed call, while the serving layer calls `parse_streaming_increment` once per delta with no end-of-stream flush, so a second call already sitting in the buffer would have been stranded had the last delta carried it.

## Modifications

- Match the first complete call in the buffer with lazy quantifiers (`(.*?)`) instead of the last.
- Loop until the buffer drains: every complete call already buffered is emitted in the same increment, with correct monotonic `tool_index`.

The two open PRs referenced in the issue (#42328 at 4581069, #42464 at 72cbf05) were verified by the reporter to still drop the first call; this PR fixes the root cause instead of patching the symptom. Closing the loop in the detector keeps `detect_and_parse` and streaming semantics aligned.

## Accuracy Tests

New regression test `TestDeepSeekV3Detector::test_parse_streaming_two_complete_calls_in_one_increment`: a single increment holding two complete calls must emit both with correct names, arguments, and indices. Verified red without the fix (first call missing) and green with it.

Local run (CPU-only, parser imports only): `pytest test/registered/function_call/test_function_call_parser.py::TestDeepSeekV3Detector` — both V3 tests pass. The issue's exact repro script now prints both calls streaming-side, matching `detect_and_parse`.

Note: the seven `TestDeepSeekV32Detector` failures in the same file reproduce on current main without this change (separate pre-existing issue, untouched here). No GPU available locally; parser-level coverage only, CI covers the rest.

nodes.body:
@he-yufeng this fixes #43523. Only the conflict is in the way. The branch sits on `05e4092` from March, and main has since moved the parser tests to `test/registered/unit/function_call/`. It needs a rebase onto main before it can merge.

```
$ python repro.py     # the script from #43523, CPython 3.12, CPU only
# base 05e4092
streaming:     [(0, 'get_tourist_attractions')]
# head fde0db2
streaming:     [(0, 'get_weather'), (0, None), (1, 'get_tourist_attractions'), (1, None)]
  args:        [(0, '{"city": "Paris"}'), (1, '{"city": "Tokyo"}')]

$ python -m pytest test/registered/function_call/test_function_call_parser.py -q
# base 05e4092: 145 passed
# head fde0db2: 146 passed
# head test, deepseekv3_detector.py from 05e4092: 1 failed, 145 passed
FAILED ...::TestDeepSeekV3Detector::test_parse_streaming_two_complete_calls_in_one_increment

$ patch -p5 deepseekv3_detector.py < head.diff     # onto main 0a21a3b: applies clean
$ python -m pytest test/registered/unit/function_call/test_function_call_parser.py -q
# main 0a21a3b: 15 failed, 235 passed     # main with the head detector: the same 15 failed, 235 passed
# the 15 are DeepSeekV32/V4 tests that need torchvision, absent here
```

blocking: the rebase, with the new test moved into `test/registered/unit/function_call/test_function_call_parser.py`.

#43553 is a second fix for #43523, so which one lands is the maintainers' call. @JustinTong0323, could you take the review after the rebase?

files.patch:
@@ -111,12 +111,20 @@ def parse_streaming_increment(
 
         calls: list[ToolCallItem] = []
         try:
-            partial_match = re.search(
-                pattern=r"<｜tool▁call▁begin｜>(.*)<｜tool▁sep｜>(.*)\n```json\n(.*)\n```.*",
-                string=current_text,
-                flags=re.DOTALL,
-            )
-            if partial_match:
+            # Match the first complete call in the buffer, not the last: a
+            # greedy (.*) spans two coalesced calls and swallows the first one.
+            # Loop so every complete call already in the buffer is emitted in
+            # this increment (the serving layer calls us once per delta and has
+            # no end-of-stream flush).
+            while True:
+                current_text = self._buffer
+                partial_match = re.search(
+                    pattern=r"<｜tool▁call▁begin｜>(.*?)<｜tool▁sep｜>(.*?)\n```json\n(.*?)\n```.*",
+                    string=current_text,
+                    flags=re.DOTALL,
+                )
+                if not partial_match:
+                    break
                 func_name = partial_match.group(2).strip()
                 func_args_raw = partial_match.group(3).strip()
 
@@ -189,11 +197,13 @@ def parse_streaming_increment(
                         else:
                             self._buffer = ""
 
-                        result = StreamingParseResult(normal_text="", calls=calls)
                         self.current_tool_id += 1
                         self._last_arguments = ""
                         self.current_tool_name_sent = False
-                        return result
+                        # The buffer may already hold the next complete call.
+                        continue
+                    # Arguments still streaming in; wait for the next delta.
+                    break
 
             return StreamingParseResult(normal_text="", calls=calls)

@@ -1248,6 +1248,26 @@ def test_parse_streaming_multiple_tool_calls_with_multi_token_chunk(self):
         self.assertEqual(params1["city"], "Shanghai")
         self.assertEqual(params2["city"], "Beijing")
 
+    def test_parse_streaming_two_complete_calls_in_one_increment(self):
+        """A coalesced backlog holding two complete calls must emit both (#43523)."""
+        text = (
+            "<｜tool▁calls▁begin｜>"
+            "<｜tool▁call▁begin｜>function<｜tool▁sep｜>get_weather\n"
+            '```json\n{"city": "Paris"}\n```<｜tool▁call▁end｜>'
+            "\n<｜tool▁call▁begin｜>function<｜tool▁sep｜>get_tourist_attractions\n"
+            '```json\n{"city": "Tokyo"}\n```<｜tool▁call▁end｜>'
+            "<｜tool▁calls▁end｜>"
+        )
+
+        result = self.detector.parse_streaming_increment(text, self.tools)
+        names = [c.name for c in result.calls if c.name]
+        args = [json.loads(c.parameters) for c in result.calls if c.parameters]
+        indices = [c.tool_index for c in result.calls]
+
+        self.assertEqual(names, ["get_weather", "get_tourist_attractions"])
+        self.assertEqual(args, [{"city": "Paris"}, {"city": "Tokyo"}])
+        self.assertEqual(indices, [0, 0, 1, 1])
